reference_solution: Store sorted starts and parallel immutable window records. Bisect on start for insertion. The predecessor overlaps when its end is greater than the new start; the successor overlaps when its start is less than the new end. For lookup, bisect-right on starts and inspect the predecessor using `start <= timestamp < end`.
explanation: Sorted non-overlapping intervals mean only neighboring entries can conflict with a new interval. Half-open boundaries allow adjacent windows without ambiguity and let consecutive evaluation cohorts share a boundary timestamp safely.

alternatives.name: Interval tree
alternatives.solution: Use an augmented balanced tree keyed by starts and maximum ends.
advantages: supports overlapping intervals and richer queries
disadvantages: not in the Python standard library

trade_off_analysis: List insertion is O(n), while point lookup is O(log n).
Returning immutable tuples protects invariants but copies the outer collection.
A production schedule should be versioned for reproducible evaluation reports.

complexity.expected_time: add is O(n) due to list insertion after O(log n) search; find is O(log n).

testing_and_debugging: Test touching, nested, partial, and exact duplicate intervals.
Test start inclusion, end exclusion, gaps, infinities, and NaN.
production_follow_ups: Version complete schedules and attach evaluation runs to a version.
Use a persistent tree if updates and snapshots dominate.
strong_response_example: I will use two parallel lists sorted by start. Bisect gives the insertion point; only predecessor.end > start and successor.start < end can overlap. Lookup uses bisect_right and checks the predecessor with a half-open comparison.
